answer: In a decentralized system, dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect punishment matrices provide a sonnet-like structure to guarantee strict Nash equilibrium against Sybil multiplication, akin to the lotus effect where a single perturbation prevents the formation of a monolithic entity. By imposing a fine on every action, a haven of Nash equilibrium is created where no agent can benefit from multiplying their identity, thus preventing the exploitation of the system by a single entity.
